get.description: Returns validated extracted filing rules from active source documents, newest first. Use this for e-filing, service, fee, timing, courtesy copy, and courtroom preference rules in any court we cover. Results are paged: meta.total is the number of matching rules, and meta.next_offset is the offset of the next page (null on the last page). Searches with q or case_type examine at most 10,000 candidate rules, which covers any single court; narrow broader searches with district_id, judge_slug, logic_type, or workflow_phase.

post.description:
Runs the deterministic lint engine against the provided document metadata and filing context.
Returns structured compliance results with per-rule pass/fail status.

Only `page_count` and `word_count` are required in the document object.
Omitted optional sections cause their corresponding checks to be silently skipped.

warnings.description: Conditions that may affect result completeness. Present only when something noteworthy occurred.

422.description: The court has no compliance profile yet; read its rules with /rules or /extracted-rules

429.description: Rate limit exceeded (60 requests per minute)

500.description: Failed to fetch data from database

post.summary: Classify a PDF document for compliance checking
post.description:
Upload a PDF and receive document classification (scope, motion type) plus a partial request body for POST /check. The response includes a `supported` boolean: `true` for classifiable federal court filings, `false` (with `confidence: "low"`) for state court forms, blank templates, or non-legal documents. The check_request includes judge, district, scope, and document metadata; you must add is_pro_se, pmc_completed, opposing_party_pro_se, and filing_role before sending to /check.

May take 10-30 seconds to respond.

200.description: Classification results with partial check request (add filing context fields before sending to /check)

422.description: The court has no compliance profile yet (read its rules with /rules or /extracted-rules), or the PDF could not be read: it is password-protected, is not a valid PDF, or has scanned pages that text recognition rejected. `scanned_pages` lists the 1-based page numbers that needed text recognition.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded (5 requests per minute)

500.description: Internal error while reading the PDF

503.description: The PDF has scanned pages and text recognition is unavailable. Text-based PDFs are not affected. `scanned_pages` lists the 1-based page numbers that needed it.
